summary: Ingress NLB preserving client source IP causes intermittent mTLS revalidation failures and streaming disconnects
description:
Issue summary: After a config change on the customer's ingress Network Load Balancer (NLB) to 'preserve client source IP' for compliance logging, FluxPay reports intermittent mTLS handshake failures and streaming connection disconnects from their private deployment.
Impact: customer-facing streaming endpoints (chat/stream) see 5xx errors and disconnects for ~3-8% of requests during morning batch windows, causing user-visible interruptions and failed token refreshes.
Environment: FluxPay private deployment in prod-us-west (VPC peered to Redwood control plane).
Recent change: customer's infra team enabled source IP preservation and proxy-protocol v2 in front of Redwood serving nodes.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady streaming requests through NLB with source-ip-preserve enabled. 2) Observe a subset of connections reset during TLS client-certificate revalidation (every ~30-120s). 3) Capture conntrack and packet traces on a serving node during a failure window.
Observed behavior: TLS handshake reset mid-stream (RST), followed by control-plane auth retries and KV-cache invalidation on serving node. Logs indicate "client cert validation failed: origin IP mismatch" in the serving node auth layer and high conntrack churn on the on-prem firewall.
Expected behavior: preserving client IP should not break mTLS lifecycle or long-lived GRPC streams; mTLS revalidation should succeed and connections should remain stable.
Logs/metrics: - Serving node logs: repeated "client-cert revalidation: peer-ip changed" and "stream terminated: tls handshake error". - Control plane traces: increased auth latency spikes (p99 +150ms) correlated with failures. - Network captures: TCP teardown (RST) immediately after cert revalidation attempt, conntrack entries showing simultaneous SNAT rewrite at egress appliance. - CloudWatch/Prometheus: streaming disconnect rate spike from 2% -> 6% at 2024-10-28T09:20Z.
Workaround attempted: customer temporarily disabled source-ip-preserve on NLB and re-enabled default SNAT; error rate dropped back to baseline.
Impact window: intermittent across multiple AZs but concentrated where egress middlebox path included legacy firewall with aggressive conntrack timeouts.
comments: 2024-10-28 10:05 - Support (Samantha Lee): Triage complete. Customer provided packet captures and NLB config. Observed proxy-protocol v2 plus client IP preservation. Opening network investigation with infra/SRE.

2024-10-28 12:40 - SRE (Marco Ruiz): Found conntrack churn on customer's firewall correlated to failure windows. Hypothesis: preserving source IP prevents expected SNAT behavior; downstream egress middlebox rewrites ports causing TLS session peer mismatch during mTLS revalidation (cert bound to IP:port).

2024-10-28 15:10 - Customer (FluxPay-network): Confirmed we changed NLB to preserve source IP for audit logs yesterday. Rolling back to SNAT immediately reduced errors. Can we recommend a stable config so we can keep source IPs for logs?

2024-10-29 09:02 - Support (Samantha Lee): Noted customer's need for client IP visibility. Proposed solution: enable proxy-protocol v2 end-to-end and configure Redwood ingress to consume proxy-protocol while keeping internal SNAT consistent for mTLS validation, or maintain SNAT and use X-Forwarded-For for logging.

2024-10-30 11:20 - Eng (Diego Alvarez): Applied a canary config on dedicated canary targets: accept proxy-protocol v2 and use the proxy-provided source for app-level logging but perform mTLS validation against the annotated connection id rather than raw peer IP. Monitoring canary for 4 hours.
2024-10-30 15:45 - Support (Marco Ruiz): Canary metrics stable. Streaming disconnects remained within baseline. Preparing rollout plan and runbook updates.
investigation_notes: Packet analysis: SYN/ACK exchange normal; TLS ClientHello from preserved IP arrives, server initiates revalidation and the egress firewall rewrites source port and occasionally performs asymmetric NAT, causing server-side TLS session mapping to fail.
Auth subsystem logs: certificate/connexion binding currently compares subject + (peer_ip:peer_port) on revalidation. This is brittle when fronting appliances rewrite ports for long-lived connections.

Conntrack observations: customer's on-prem firewall had conntrack timeouts tuned low and aggressive port reuse; when NLB preserved source IP, backend saw inconsistent 5-tuple between initial handshake and later revalidation probes.
Repro script created by SRE to simulate NLB-preserve + firewall SNAT behavior; reproduces ~4% stream resets matching customer report. Script and pcap uploaded to linked PR for review.
Risk analysis: wholesale disabling of source IP at customer side is unacceptable to them. Need a solution that preserves their auditability while keeping mTLS integrity and stream stability.
resolution: Short-term workaround: customer rolled back to SNAT on NLB which reduced errors immediately. Documented as mitigation in ticket.

Middle-term fix implemented in canary: - Enable proxy-protocol v2 on NLB target group. - Redwood ingress configured to parse proxy-protocol and record original client IP for logs. - Serving auth code changed to bind certs to connection identifier (connection-id + certificate fingerprint) instead of raw peer_ip:peer_port. This avoids port-rewrite breakage. See PR #1457.

Rollout notes: Canary (10% traffic) for 6 hours then 50% then 100% across us-west. Monitoring dashboards for stream disconnect rate, auth latency, and conntrack resets created and added to Redwood Console (dashboards/streaming-mtls-revalidation).

Postmortem actions: - Add runbook entry for customers considering source-ip preservation (NLB best-practices). - Update private-deploy onboarding checklist to recommend proxy-protocol + logging vs source ip preserve. - Reach out to FluxPay CS to schedule follow-up to validate audit logs and ensure no regression.

Customer remediation: FluxPay accepted proxy-protocol approach and validated that audit logs now include original client IP with no increase in streaming disconnects. Ticket to remain open for 7 days monitoring before closure.
